key_insight: TESS replaces brittle per-sample weighting with a transferable selection network, but it must be trained with a new pointwise value matching loss to avoid unstable optimization and poor generalization.
engineering_relevance: For large-scale language model data curation, this offers a scalable way to learn reusable selection policies that transfer across datasets, corpus sizes, and model scales.
method: Build a selection network instead of assigning independent weights to each example
Train it with Pointwise Value Matching (PVM) to match example-level utility signals
Use the learned scorer for transferable data selection across subsets and full corpora
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on LLM safety and targeted instruction tuning, with transfer from subsets to full corpora and from smaller to larger models.
watch_item: Directly inserting a selection network into existing MTS objectives can suppress weights and overfit to easy features, so the loss design is critical.
paper_title: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)
